findings.passage: Representative Louderback voted for SJR 37, which proposed a constitutional amendment clarifying that voters must be US citizens.
findings.note: Under the heading ELECTION INTEGRITY on his campaign site's 89th-session accomplishments page (undated; it refers to the amendments on the November 4 ballot, so late 2025). A statement issued by his campaign about his own vote on SJR 37.

Louderback is listed as a joint author (with the lead author) of a bill on disclosure of a candidate's citizenship for public office. Referred to the Elections committee 2025-04-03; no later action shown.

findings.motion: coauthor of HB 5337, proof of citizenship to register to vote (filed 2025-03-14; date Louderback was added not shown)
findings.note: Louderback is listed as a coauthor of the bill requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote, with criminal offenses. The House Elections committee report was sent to Calendars on 2025-05-07; no floor action is shown.

findings.motion: House cosponsor of SB 16, proof of citizenship to register to vote (bill filed 2025-03-11; date Louderback was added not shown)
findings.note: Louderback is listed as a House cosponsor of the Senate bill requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote, including a limited federal ballot for a voter who cannot supply the proof. The House committee report was sent to Calendars on 2025-05-25.

findings.motion: coauthor of HB 5138, attorney general duty to prosecute election-law offenses (filed 2025-03-13; date Louderback was added not shown)
findings.note: Louderback is listed as a coauthor of a bill on the attorney general's duty to prosecute criminal offenses under the state's election laws. The last action shown is the Senate appointing conferees on 2025-05-29.

findings.motion: coauthor of HJR 189, constitutional amendment on attorney general authority to prosecute election-law offenses (filed 2025-03-12; date Louderback was added not shown)
findings.note: Louderback is listed as a coauthor of a proposed constitutional amendment specifying the attorney general's authority to prosecute election-law offenses. Referred to State Affairs 2025-04-02; no later action shown.

findings.motion: co sponsor, House Committee Report (C.S.H.B. 5337; no engrossed or enrolled version exists)
findings.note: Listed as co of TX-HB-5337-2025 on the official Texas Legislature authors page (identity step 2026-10-28: printed name matched to one 89th Legislature member of that chamber, then to the roster by surname and first initial).
